idea.name: Lawn care quote generator
idea.one_liner: Give lawn care businesses an instant pricing tool that captures homeowner leads; use it as a free lead magnet for possible paid add-ons.
idea.customer: Lawn care businesses and homeowners seeking mowing or hedging quotes.
idea.offer: A web app that estimates lawn care prices from property details, shows an instant quote, and sends the lead details to the business.
idea.revenue_model: Suggested as a free lead magnet and foot in the door to charge for other services; exact pricing is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: So, they're losing money ignoring calls from people that want a price because they're probably already very targeted and like it's probably a very hot lead that they're ignoring, right?
which is transparency of pricing upfront and speed to reply.
So, the information, the lead form just goes to my Google sheet.

claims.claim: A test quote generated by the app was $7.80 per service using mock pricing data.
claims.quote: It gave me the quote, which is $7.80 per service because it doesn't have any real data.

claims.claim: One demo pricing setup used 50 bucks per 1,000 square feet of mowing.
claims.quote: So, I just chose 50 bucks per thousand square feet of mowing.

claims.claim: The demo added 25% for hedging.
claims.quote: I said if they want hedging too just add a 25% additional cost.

claims.claim: The demo applied 5% discounts for monthly, bi-weekly, and weekly service selections.
claims.quote: if the customer signs up for monthly instead of one time they get a 5% discount bi-weekly an additional 5% discount. and then weekly an additional 5% discount.

claims.claim: One app formula used 43,500 square feet per acre.
claims.quote: I need to know the acreage and I told emergent or I just reminded it like you know we're using acreage as like 43,500 square feet per acre, right?

claims.claim: A separate formula subtracted 10% of the acreage from the square footage.
claims.quote: And then I also told it subtract 10% of the acreage from the square footage as well.

claims.claim: A demo estimate used 1.6 cents per square foot to reach about 40–50 bucks for a small lot.
claims.quote: So I just said multiply the the square footage by 1.6 cents because that's about how you get to about 40 50 bucks, right?

claims.claim: For larger lawns, the speaker instructed the app to discount the 1.6-cent rate by 20% for every quarter acre.
claims.quote: A half acre lawn and 2,000 foot house should not cost 281. Your math is right, but that price is way too expensive. Okay, so like do a discount against the 1.6 cent rate of 20% for every quarter acre.

claims.claim: The app was instructed to charge full price once per month, 20% off for twice monthly, and 40% off for three or more visits.
claims.quote: And then I said add a field for asking how many mos per month if once full price twice equals 20% off the total per mo three or more equals 40% off the total per mo per mo.

claims.claim: The configured minimum was $40 per month, with an optional weed-eating add-on set at 20% of the monthly total.
claims.quote: I said work in a minimum where it will never quote any job less than $40 per mo. It will override all math and then add in a check box that says add in weed eating for insert price more per mo and then the price should be 20% of the total mo amount.

claims.claim: A sample calculation with a 0.1-acre lot estimated roughly 4,300 square feet.
claims.quote: So let's just say it's a 0.1 acre lot. That's roughly 4,300 square f feet.

claims.claim: The initial prompt specified 4592 per cut using a 1.6-cent-per-square-foot formula.
claims.quote: So, the quote should be 4592 per cut, which is 4,300 minus 1,000US 430 multiplied by 1.6 cents per net square feet of lot.

claims.claim: The speaker estimated that adding a question could reduce responses by 5%.
claims.quote: Like I could add that question in and I might get 5% fewer responses because it's more friction, you know, right?

claims.claim: A sample app quote showed 2,000 square feet at 112 bucks.
claims.quote: 2,000 square feet, 112 bucks. Discount applied.

claims.claim: A lead sheet showed a quote of $112.50 with contact information.
claims.quote: And so, now, you know, the $112.50 is there along with their contact info.

claims.claim: A proposed follow-up example offered to reduce an $80 weekly quote to $75 if service started that week.
claims.quote: It's, you know, the quote says it would be 80 bucks uh a week, but actually if if we start this week, I'll do it for 75.

claims.claim: One app returned a quote of $2450 per service for a one-acre lawn scenario.
claims.quote: Your custom quote, $2450 per service. So, that's a lot.

claims.claim: Another app added 500 bucks per cut for weed eating.
claims.quote: I did want weed eating, so it adds that 500 bucks per cut.

claims.claim: A 2.2-acre test produced a $512 quote that the speaker considered too high.
claims.quote: 512 for 2.2 acres is still too much.

claims.claim: The speakers said the prototype apps could be live and working in under an hour.
claims.quote: will have something live and working in the span of under an hour as well.

claims.claim: The speaker proposed sending a link by text if a call went unanswered and the text was not answered in five minutes.
claims.quote: if the text isn't answered in 5 minutes then auto text a link to this and say so sorry I'm actually mowing a lawn right now

claims.claim: Keeping the app on Emergent would cost $20 per month, and launching the apps cost about $10.
claims.quote: If we wanted to keep this app on emergent, it would cost 20 bucks a month. Or we could export it and take it somewhere else. But it cost us about about 10 bucks to launch these apps.

acquisition_channels.details: The hosts shared prototype links and a Twitter poll, and invited landscaping business owners to try an app; no paying-customer results are stated.

ideas.delivery: A hosted web app calculates a quote from lawn size, service type, and frequency, then captures contact details in a form and sends them to Google Sheets. The lawn care operator follows up with the lead.

prices: Demo mowing rate: 50 bucks per 1,000 square feet
Frequency discounts: 5% increments; another model used 20% or 40% monthly discounts
Weed eating: 20% of monthly total in one model
Emergent: $20 per month; about $10 to launch the demo apps

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to names, phone numbers, and property details collected by the form. PECR applies to marketing texts; obtain valid consent where required. Cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS. The described text and call follow-up is in response to a quote inquiry.
